documents.title: H&P - Admission - Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 23:40, ED bay 4
CC: cough, fever, new confusion
HPI:
66F brought to ED by son for 4 days of productive cough, subjective fevers, and progressive dyspnea.
Son reports new confusion today - patient is normally independent, drives, manages her own medications and finances.
On arrival pt oriented to self only; could not state location or month.
Son denies falls, head trauma, alcohol use, or missed medications.
Cough productive of rust-colored sputum. Pleuritic right-sided chest pain with deep breath.
Two episodes of nonbloody vomiting in ED; unable to keep down water or pills.
No sick contacts known to son. No recent travel. No hemoptysis, no leg swelling.
ED COURSE / TRIAGE VITALS:
T 38.9 C, HR 112, BP 86/54, respiratory rate 32 at triage, SpO2 87% on RA.
Placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93% within 10 min.
Hypotension to 86/54 at triage treated with 2 L normal saline bolus; BP after fluids 96/58.
Repeat at 4 hours: respiratory rate 30, HR 98, T 38.1 C, SpO2 93% on 3L NC.
Lactate 2.6 -> 1.8 after fluids. Blood cultures x2 drawn before antibiotics.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin 500 mg started in ED at 22:15.
PMH:
HTN, type 2 DM (diet controlled), hypothyroidism, osteoarthritis, prior cholecystectomy.
HOME MEDS:
amlodipine 5 mg daily, levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, acetaminophen PRN, cholecalciferol 1000 units daily.
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL: lives alone in a single-story home, son lives 10 min away, nonsmoker for 20 yrs (prior 15 pack-yr), no alcohol.
FAMILY HX: father MI age 70, mother CVA.
ROS: per HPI, limited by confusion; son supplements. No dysuria, no diarrhea, no rash.
EXAM:
Gen: ill-appearing, mildly diaphoretic, answers simple questions slowly.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no JVD.
Neuro: oriented to self only, follows one-step commands, no focal deficit, no nuchal rigidity.
Lungs: coarse crackles right base and right mid-lung, egophony RLL, dullness to percussion right base.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, cap refill 3 sec.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Ext: no edema, warm after fluids.
Skin: no rash, no cellulitis.
LABS ON ARRIVAL:
WBC 17.8 K with 88% neutrophils, Hgb 12.4, Plt 231.
BUN 34 mg/dL, sodium 127 mEq/L on arrival. Creatinine 1.42, K 3.9, bicarb 20, glucose 168.
AST 34, ALT 28, albumin 3.1, total bili 0.8.
Procalcitonin 4.6. Influenza PCR negative. Resp viral panel pending.
IMAGING:
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion.
Effusion too small to sample at this time.
ASSESSMENT:
66F with severe community-acquired pneumonia, multilobar right-sided, complicated by hypoxemic respiratory failure, encephalopathy, hypovolemic/septic physiology, AKI and hyponatremia.
CURB-65 of 3 (confusion, BUN >19 mg/dL, respiratory rate >=30) - supports inpatient admission with close monitoring.
PLAN:
1. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin.
2. O2 to keep SpO2 >92%, currently 3L NC; wean as tolerated.
3. Continuous pulse ox, telemetry, vitals q4h; MAP goal >65.
4. Additional 500 mL NS if MAP <65 or UOP <0.5 mL/kg/hr; strict I/O.
5. NPO to sips while vomiting; ondansetron 4 mg IV q6h PRN; IV maintenance fluids with sodium recheck q8h.
6. Hold amlodipine given soft pressures. Continue levothyroxine IV equivalent while NPO.
7. Repeat CBC/BMP in AM, follow blood cultures, sputum Gram stain and culture, strep/legionella urinary antigens.
8. Incentive spirometry q1h while awake, HOB elevated, aspiration precautions.
9. Delirium precautions, reorientation, avoid sedating meds, RN sitter check q2h.
10. Admit to stepdown telemetry. Discussed with son at bedside; escalation to ICU if increasing O2 need.
Attending notified 23:55; agrees with plan.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:15
Subjective:
Pt more interactive overnight; now oriented to self, place, and knows it is morning. Son at bedside states she sounds more like herself.
Confusion improving but not resolved - still intermittently repeats questions.
Reports right-sided chest soreness with cough. Vomited x1 at 04:30 after attempting crackers.
Overnight: no fever spike after 02:00, no respiratory distress events, RN notes 1 episode of desaturation to 89% when NC displaced, corrected with repositioning.
Objective:
T 37.4 C, HR 88, BP 108/64, RR 24, SpO2 93% on 3L NC - still on 3L NC on hospital day 2.
UOP 1150 mL over 12 hrs. Net +1.6 L.
Exam: alert, no accessory muscle use. Crackles persist right base and right mid-lung; decreased breath sounds right base. Mucous membranes moist. No edema.
Labs this AM: WBC 13.1, Hgb 11.8, Plt 224, Na 131, K 4.1, BUN 26, Cr 1.08, bicarb 22.
Lactate 1.2. Blood cultures no growth at 12 hrs. Strep and legionella urinary antigens negative. Sputum Gram stain: GPC in pairs.
Assessment/Plan:
Severe multilobar CAP - clinically improving; still oxygen dependent.
1. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin - unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting, so no PO conversion today.
2. O2: attempt wean to 2L NC with ambulation trial with RN/RT this morning; hold wean if SpO2 <90%.
3. Antiemetic scheduled ondansetron 4 mg IV q8h; small sips clears only.
4. Continue IV fluids at 75 mL/hr; recheck Na this afternoon given 127 on arrival, now 131.
5. Hyponatremia and AKI both improving with hydration.
6. Continue delirium precautions and reorientation; PT eval ordered for gait safety.
7. Incentive spirometry q1h, flutter valve.
8. Follow small right pleural effusion clinically; no indication for thoracentesis, no increasing dyspnea.
9. Resume amlodipine when BP consistently >110 systolic and PO tolerated.
Discussed trajectory with pt and son; goal is oxygen wean and tolerating oral intake before discharge.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 15:40 (interval/afternoon)
Subjective:
Pt sat in chair 45 min, tolerated broth and 200 mL apple juice at 13:00 without emesis - first tolerated intake this admission.
No vomiting since 04:30. Cough less painful. Denies dyspnea at rest.
Fully oriented this afternoon - name, place, situation; son confirms baseline mentation. Confusion resolved.
Objective:
14:00 vitals: T 37.1 C, HR 82, BP 116/70, RR 20, SpO2 94% on 2L NC.
Ambulation trial 120 ft with RN: SpO2 nadir 91% on 2L NC, HR 104, no dyspnea reported.
Wean trial to RA at 14:30: SpO2 fell to 89% after 4 min, returned to 3L NC per RT, SpO2 94%. Remains 3L NC at rest.
Afternoon labs: Na 134, K 4.0, BUN 21, Cr 0.96, WBC 11.4.
Blood cultures no growth at 18 hrs. Respiratory viral panel negative.
Exam: crackles right base, less coarse than AM. No respiratory distress. Abdomen soft.
Assessment/Plan:
Severe CAP, improving. Oxygen requirement persists at 3L NC; mentation and hemodynamics normalized.
1. Third dose ceftriaxone 1 g IV given 14:00 with azithromycin IV; will transition to oral regimen at discharge now that PO tolerated this afternoon.
2. Advance to soft diet this evening; continue ondansetron PRN only.
3. Home oxygen 3L NC arranged with delivery this evening; RT completed teaching with pt and son, pulse oximeter provided.
4. PT cleared for ambulation with cane, no fall precautions beyond baseline.
5. Discharge planned later today with son staying overnight at her home for 48 hrs.
6. Resume amlodipine 5 mg daily at discharge.
7. Follow-up chest imaging and clinic visit in 5 to 7 days; return precautions reviewed.
Attending saw and examined pt at 15:20, agrees with discharge later today.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission: HD1. Discharge: HD2, 18:20. Length of stay 2 days.
Discharge diagnosis: Severe community-acquired pneumonia, multilobar right-sided, with hypoxemic respiratory failure, acute encephalopathy, AKI, and hyponatremia - all improved.
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:
66F presented with 4 days of productive cough, fever, dyspnea, and new confusion per son, who reports patient is normally independent; oriented to self only on arrival.
Triage vitals notable for SpO2 87% on RA at triage; placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%. Respiratory rate 32 at triage, 30 at 4 hours.
Hypotension to 86/54 at triage; 2 L normal saline given; BP after fluids 96/58.
Initial labs: WBC 17.8, BUN 34 mg/dL, sodium 127 mEq/L on arrival, Cr 1.42, lactate 2.6.
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion. Effusion small, no drainage indicated.
CURB-65 of 3 documented in the admitting note; admitted to stepdown telemetry.
Treated with ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin; unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, so antibiotics remained IV until the afternoon of HD2.
Sputum Gram stain showed gram-positive cocci in pairs. Blood cultures no growth at discharge. Influenza PCR, respiratory viral panel, strep and legionella urinary antigens all negative.
Mentation returned to baseline by HD2 afternoon; fully oriented and confirmed at baseline by son.
Hyponatremia corrected to 134 and creatinine improved to 0.96 with IV fluids.
Oxygen weaning attempted twice; still on 3L NC on hospital day 2 with desaturation to 89% on room air, so discharged with home oxygen 3L NC and pulse oximeter after RT teaching.
Tolerated broth and juice at 13:00 on HD2 without emesis and advanced to soft diet.
DISCHARGE VITALS: T 37.0 C, HR 80, BP 118/72, RR 18, SpO2 94% on 3L NC.
DISCHARGE EXAM: alert and fully oriented, comfortable, crackles right base, no accessory muscle use, ambulates 120 ft with cane.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Oral respiratory antibiotic course to complete total 7 days as prescribed at discharge.
2. Amlodipine 5 mg PO daily - resumed.
3. Levothyroxine 75 mcg PO daily.
4. Ondansetron 4 mg PO q8h PRN nausea, 12 tablets.
5. Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN pain or fever.
6. Cholecalciferol 1000 units daily.
EQUIPMENT: home oxygen concentrator 3L NC with portable tank, pulse oximeter, incentive spirometer, cane.
INSTRUCTIONS:
Use oxygen continuously; check pulse ox twice daily and record. Do not remove oxygen for walking.
Incentive spirometry 10 breaths per hour while awake. Increase fluids as tolerated.
Son to stay at patient's home for the next 48 hrs; he has been instructed on warning signs.
RETURN/CALL IMMEDIATELY IF: SpO2 below 90% on oxygen, new confusion, temperature above 38.3 C, worsening chest pain, repeated vomiting, or inability to drink fluids.
FOLLOW-UP:
Primary care clinic in 5 to 7 days for repeat exam, BMP, and oxygen reassessment.
Repeat chest imaging in 6 to 8 weeks to confirm resolution of infiltrate and effusion.
Pneumococcal and seasonal vaccination to be addressed as outpatient once recovered.
Discharge instructions reviewed with pt and son at bedside; both verbalized understanding. Attending available by phone.
